correctness.rationale: Checked all-agent all-good EFX quantifiers including removal of a zero-valued other-spoke good. Their exact reductions give S+1>=max Xi and Xi>=Yi-1{other center edges absent}. For m>3R+2, the center-versus-dominant-leaf constraint forces dominant center inventory >R, reducing each subsidiary leaf to its balanced binomial threshold. The finite exact central binomial slice includes the odd-m exceptional point; boundary cases (Y=0, parity, empty bundles) were tested. Global Gaussian limits follow from concentration of aggregate subsidiary center goods, conditional on the product of symmetric-majority events, and CLT. Uniform local binomial estimates plus diverging subsidiary total establish the sharp subcritical equivalent. Standalone pure-Python checker executed: 85 multistar exact bundle-deletion comparisons plus exact finite dominant-slice comparisons. Finite tests are not cited as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The existence of a fair graph orientation says nothing quantitative about whether independent non-wasteful random assignments will meet EFX. The theorem solves a natural robustness probability for the multistar family singled out by recent orientation-existence theory, exposes an exact finite event that respects zero-valued goods, and identifies a sharp square-root total-supply window and subcritical constant. This separates deterministic existence from typical randomized performance; fixed-k highly unbalanced multiplicities are motivated by a dominant bilateral asset relationship and multiple weaker relationships, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
